findings.text: follow-on (record, not code): the reviewed run's negative-control log is green. At revision 8b50e5ba it records `-k negating_the_equilibrium_field` as `1 passed, 20 deselected` with `EXIT=0`, i.e. the test PASSED against the negated store. The red-log admission rule wants a non-zero EXIT= and at least one failing test id, so this log does not by itself demonstrate that a mutation breaks the guard. Non-blocking: the change is correct and this review supplied the missing falsification (mutating the reader to np.abs the toroidal field reddens the q-relation test, FAILED EXIT=1).

follow-on: the channel-consensus check was changed to unanimity (`0 < row.raw_flux_loop_opposite_sign_channels < row.raw_flux_loop_channels`): an agreeing set is silent, a split set violates. No test exercises the one-loop (opposite == 0) case as a non-violation, so reverting to the all-negative form `!=` leaves the suite green (21 passed) while changing whether a single-absolute-loop observation scores. The consensus change is the one that makes JT-60SA's single absolute loop score at all.

follow-on: _aligned_loop now tolerates a gap of up to one sampling interval (`tolerance = resolution; if low > current_low + tolerance`). No test pins the newly-accepted case: the resampling test covers a fully-covering shifted grid and the refusal test still refuses a 1.5 s gap, so reverting the tolerance to strict leaves the file green (21 passed).

justifications.fit: The change extends ShotSignObservation, score_convention and the existing reader rather than adding a mechanism.
